scope: NC+CM methodology-focused: calibration / external validation / fairness / leakage / generalization on clinical binary cohorts

candidates.title: Detecting shortcut learning for fair medical AI using shortcut testing
candidates.scope_hint: Multitask-learning method to test for shortcut learning as a fairness driver, applied to clinical radiology and dermatology classification tasks; directly relevant to leakage/shortcut gates
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Demonstration tasks include imaging (radiology/dermatology) but the paper's contribution is methodology not imaging-primary

candidates.title: Predicting pediatric patient rehabilitation outcomes after spinal deformity surgery with artificial intelligence
candidates.scope_hint: Retrospective multi-site cohort (455 patients, 2 hospitals); 6 ML models for post-op outcome prediction with explicit confidence calibration and algorithmic-fairness mitigation; uses radiographic features as inputs but task is outcome prediction not imaging classification
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Outcome may be multi-class/continuous SRS-22R rather than strictly binary; verify before extraction

candidates.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence and human-based prediction and stratification of the risk of long-term kidney allograft failure
candidates.scope_hint: Retrospective cohort of 400 transplant recipients; AI vs 9 transplant physicians on long-term graft survival risk stratification; calibration and risk-stratification methodology lessons
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Outcome is graft failure (time-to-event) not strict binary; methodology framing is risk stratification

candidates.title: Acquisition parameters influence AI recognition of race in chest x-rays and mitigating these factors reduces underdiagnosis bias
candidates.scope_hint: Demographics-independent calibration strategy reduces underdiagnosis bias; fairness mitigation methodology demonstrated on chest x-ray binary diagnosis datasets
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Imaging-primary (CXR) - borderline; included because focus is bias mitigation methodology not imaging model design

candidates.title: Machine learning based early warning system enables accurate mortality risk prediction for COVID-19
candidates.scope_hint: Retrospective binary mortality prediction; ensemble of 4 ML methods; internal + 2 external validation cohorts with reported AUCs; classic external-validation case study
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Suspiciously high AUCs (~0.96) on COVID early-pandemic data may itself be a leakage cautionary tale - good for KB

candidates.title: Collider bias undermines our understanding of COVID-19 disease risk and severity
candidates.scope_hint: Methodology critique on COVID-19 risk-factor and severity studies; collider/selection bias as a leakage-adjacent failure mode for retrospective clinical risk modeling
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Conceptual paper rather than a single cohort prediction model; still extractable lessons for selection-bias gates

candidates.title: Validation of the Toronto recurrence inference using machine-learning for post-transplant hepatocellular carcinoma model
candidates.scope_hint: External validation of a published ML risk model (TRIUMPH) across 6 international centers, 2844 patients, 2000-2022; decision-curve analysis for clinical utility
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Underlying model is regularized Cox (survival); but external-validation study itself is exactly the methodology pattern MLGG cares about

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled fully automated detection of cardiac amyloidosis using electrocardiograms and echocardiograms
candidates.scope_hint: Multi-AMC training+validation; explicit deployment simulation reporting PPV/recall trade-offs and pre-screening pipelines for rare-disease binary detection
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Inputs are ECG/echo signals (signal-primary not imaging-primary); rare-disease prevalence makes PPV/recall analysis especially gate-relevant

candidates.title: Identifying and evaluating barriers for the implementation of machine learning in the intensive care unit
candidates.scope_hint: Mixed-methods: 29 interviews + quantitative experiments measuring loss from temporal drift, feature changes, data scarcity, and context-shift deployment on ICU prediction models; methodology meta-paper
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Hybrid qualitative+quantitative design; not a single binary cohort but uses multiple ICU prediction models as case studies

candidates.title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
candidates.scope_hint: Evaluates 4 algorithmic fairness criteria and their translation to long-term mortality and disparity outcomes via sociotechnical simulation grounded in AI-assisted breast cancer screening (binary)
candidates.out_of_scope_risk: Simulation-based - borderline per scope (rejects pure simulation), but grounded in real binary screening task and answers the deployment-fairness question MLGG fairness gate cares about
